findings.description: The ADR-SAG-0007 base text still says HTTP timeouts are 'configurable on backend builder for tests'. r-3 removed with_timeouts. Timeouts are now UreqTransport::new(Timeouts) construction state, passed into the backend constructor. The sprint doc's deviation table records this against ADR-SAG-0007, but the Active r-3 subsection (lines 559-585) does not say the sentence is reinterpreted or superseded. The reading 'configurable via the injected transport' is defensible, so I did not rate it BLOCKING.
findings.remediation: Add one Active r-3 bullet to ADR-SAG-0007's r-3 subsection saying timeouts (connect 10 s, request 120 s) are configured on the injected UreqTransport, which supersedes 'configurable on backend builder'. The sprint doc's frontmatter adrs/ADR text item 7 would need the same wording, since the r-3 subsection must match it verbatim. Alternatively keep it as a non-blocking note and fold it into r-3b.

gate_artifact_checks.notes: The manifest truthfully lists allowed_dependencies [sc-agent-types, ureq] (matching Cargo.toml), dependents [sc-jev, sc-jev-backends], and the test-util seam. Omitting the sc-agent-compose forbidden edge is acceptable. The header comment states why (sc-lint 0.8.0 rejects an edge to a non-member) and that r-3b adds it with the crate. This is a transient gap, not an ADR violation: no ADR names that edge as an r-3 deliverable, and a forbidden edge to an absent crate has nothing to enforce. r-3b's sprint doc must list adding it as a deliverable, which I did not verify here.

notes: Direct answers to your questions. (1) The ADR-SAG-0026 Status line and index cell read exactly 'Active (HTTP half, r-3); compose half Proposed (r-3b)'. The compose half is Proposed, and nothing in r-3 code, docs or manifests cites a compose-half bullet. The remaining compose mentions are the r-3b notes in agent-http.toml and the sc-lint.toml message (HTTP half only). (2) The ADR-0006, 0007, 0017 and 0020 r-3 subsections are Active. The ADR-0020 r-3 bullet 1 text matches the sprint doc's replacement wording with no source_scans clause. The new Proposed 'Amendment (Phase A.1, r-3b)' subsection and the index marker for ADR-0020 are present. (3) The r-3b and r-4 markers in rows 0010, 0011, 0013, 0016 and 0017 are intact. The r-1 interim cells (0008, 0009, 0014, 0019, 0022) are intact. The 0023, 0028 and 0024/0025 rows are untouched. (4) ADR-0010 added to adrs is correct. Its ureq-ownership record is what sc-lint.toml enforces, and the sc-lint.toml messages cite it. I also checked ADR-0001, 0003 and 0018 against the code, and ADR-0004 and ADR-0005 for non-regression; ADR-0004 and 0005 are not governing for this sprint and are not required in the list. (5) The code upholds ADR-0007 (BusyPolicy::default is 4 sends, 429/502/529, 30 s clamp, 1/2/4 backoff, 250 ms jitter, 90 s budget; the Retry-After grammar is a digit fold with no f64; the cancel-latency docs are accurate). It also upholds ADR-0020 (one as_str call, in expose(), under a single #[expect]; SecretHeader::matches goes through expose; no other disallowed_methods or allow( under crates/). (6) One IMPORTANT finding, ARCH-R3-001, on the ADR-0007 'configurable on backend builder' wording. Limitations: no shell was available. I confirmed branch and commit by reading .git/worktrees/r-3-shared-http/HEAD (ref sprint/r-3-shared-http) and refs/heads/sprint/r-3-shared-http (8f969ff85e09...). I did not run cargo, clippy, rg or just, so the sprint doc's reported test and lint results are not independently verified. The grep sweeps above were done with the Grep tool. I did not read the full text of docs/sc-agent-http/architecture.md, so its internal wording is unchecked beyond the ADR ids.
